global4_ranking: mean of global-aligned AP quality scores; all APs require support
limits: Controlled experimental mechanisms, not a reproduction of AutoStakkert internal algorithms.
Same 5738 observations per AP; different APs may select different frame IDs.
Pool is the 25476 PR-screened frames, not all 27689 capture frames.
Single 65px scale with 48 overlapping circular APs and fixed production 64-frame reference.
Original scalar global quality weights retained; no brightness normalization or output denoising.
Smoothing is used only to rank quality and measure alignment; original raw pixels are accumulated.
Registered variants have an extra bilinear resampling of each completed patch.
Sequential variants resample global alignment and local alignment separately.
AP overlap can increase effective frame count beyond 5738 by mixing different selections; reported frame-weight counts ignore resampling covariance.
Outside patch support, products use the original global stack.
Fine-scale variation includes real structure and artifacts; it is not a direct sensor-noise measurement.
No new AutoStakkert Global-mode stack was generated by this experiment.

validation.visual_review: Initial hard AP-support seams corrected with continuous global fallback; final local2, local2_registered and local4_sequential_registered images reviewed.

conclusions: Independent AP selection gives a measurable partial reduction of sharpened disc variation.
Changing global quality ranking, or separating global/local resampling, does not approach the AS result.
The lowest mean variation across both tested regions is patch_local2_registered, at 2.002% and 1.888%.
The strongest tested variant reduces variation 32.5% and 36.5% relative to production, but remains 3.49 and 2.94 times the AS values.
Overlap with different selected frame sets increases the effective frame-weight count; completed-patch registration also adds interpolation.
These results do not establish the cause of the remaining AS/PR gap or identify sensor noise as its origin.
